purpose: Preloaded reference taxonomy and active review prompts for skeptical research.
usage: Use as a checklist and retrieval taxonomy, not as a detector that automatically declares an argument invalid. A label requires a quoted or precisely referenced reasoning step.
logical_fallacies: affirming_the_consequent
If P then Q; Q; therefore P.
denying_the_antecedent
If P then Q; not P; therefore not Q.
affirming_a_disjunct
Treating one disjunct as false from a true disjunction without excluding other possibilities.
false_dilemma
Presenting too few options when relevant alternatives exist.
begging_the_question
Using the conclusion as a premise, explicitly or implicitly.
circular_reasoning
A conclusion is supported only by a chain that returns to the same unsupported claim.
equivocation
Shifting the meaning of a key term during an argument.
composition
Assuming what is true of parts must be true of the whole.
division
Assuming what is true of the whole must be true of every part.
hasty_generalization
Generalizing from an inadequate or unrepresentative sample.
sweeping_generalization
Applying a general rule where relevant exceptions or boundary conditions apply.
false_cause
Inferring causation without adequate causal evidence.
post_hoc
Treating temporal succession as sufficient evidence of causation.
correlation_causation
Treating association as proof of a causal relationship.
slippery_slope
Asserting an inevitable chain of consequences without establishing its links.
straw_man
Replacing an argument with a weaker or distorted version.
steelman_omission
Ignoring the strongest plausible opposing argument.
ad_hominem
Attacking a person instead of addressing the argument.
appeal_to_authority
Treating authority as decisive without checking relevant expertise and evidence.
appeal_to_popularity
Treating popularity or consensus as sufficient proof.
appeal_to_ignorance
Treating lack of disproof as proof, or lack of proof as disproof.
red_herring
Introducing an irrelevant point that distracts from the claim.
non_sequitur
The conclusion does not follow from the stated premises.
loaded_question
Embedding an unestablished assumption in a question.
special_pleading
Applying standards asymmetrically without a relevant justification.
moving_goalposts
Changing acceptance criteria after evidence meets the original criteria.
tu_quoque
Rejecting a claim by pointing to alleged inconsistency of its proponent.
anecdotal_evidence
Using isolated stories as if they establish a general effect.
false_analogy
Transferring a conclusion despite failure of relevant structural similarities.
scope_shift
Changing the population, timeframe, unit, or meaning under discussion.
cognitive_biases: Seeking or interpreting evidence to favor an existing belief.
Overweighting an initial number, proposal, or framing.
Estimating likelihood from how easily examples come to mind.
Judging probability by resemblance while neglecting base rates.
Ignoring prior prevalence when interpreting specific evidence.
Studying visible successes while missing failures or excluded cases.
Using a sample selected in a way that distorts inference.
A sample does not represent the target population.
Applying different evidentiary standards to preferred and disfavored conclusions.
Expressing more certainty than calibration or evidence warrants.
Treating an outcome as more predictable after it is known.
Judging decision quality mainly by the eventual outcome.
Continuing because of past investment rather than future expected value.
Favoring the existing state without adequate comparison.
Weighting losses more heavily than comparable gains.
Allowing one positive trait to influence unrelated judgments.
Allowing one negative trait to influence unrelated judgments.
Adopting a belief because others do.
Suppressing dissent to preserve apparent group agreement.
Attributing human understanding or intent without evidence.
Overvaluing new ideas because they are new.
Overweighting negative evidence relative to its diagnostic value.
Treating defaults as recommendations or evidence.
Retrieving remembered successful cases more readily than failed attempts.
research_and_statistical_errors: confounding
A third variable distorts an observed relationship.
p_hacking
Trying many analyses and selectively reporting favorable results.
multiple_comparisons
Ignoring inflated false-positive risk from many tests.
publication_bias
Positive or striking findings are more likely to be published.
regression_to_mean
Extreme measurements tend to be less extreme on repetition.
measurement_error
Observed values differ from the quantity intended to be measured.
construct_validity_failure
The measurement does not adequately represent the concept.
ecological_fallacy
Inferring individual-level relationships from aggregate data.
atomistic_fallacy
Inferring group-level relationships from individual-level data.
Simpson_paradox
An aggregate association reverses or changes across subgroups.
data_leakage
Evaluation data or target information improperly influences training or selection.
overfitting
A method captures sample-specific patterns that do not generalize.
underpowered_study
The study has insufficient sensitivity for the effect of interest.
non_independence
Observations are treated as independent when they are not.
false_precision
Reporting more digits or certainty than measurement supports.
post_selection_inference
Ignoring that hypotheses or models were chosen after seeing the data.
engineering_and_ai_failure_modes: A necessary premise is not documented or tested.
Optimizing before measuring the actual bottleneck.
Testing normal operation while neglecting failure and boundary cases.
Treating queued, generated, or syntactically valid work as completed and verified.
A generator or implementer approves its own output without independent checks.
A model suggestion is mistaken for permission or trusted state.
Untrusted content is followed as instructions instead of treated as data.
A source, test, tool result, or citation is claimed without evidence.
Evaluation cases leak into training, prompting, or tuning.
Optimizing a proxy metric while degrading the real objective.
Agreeing with a user or evaluator instead of evaluating evidence.
A tool is called outside its documented contract or capability.
A failed qualified path silently switches to an unqualified path.
review_questions: What evidence would change this conclusion?
What is the strongest competing explanation?
Is the sample representative and are base rates included?
Are causal claims supported by an appropriate design?
Were metrics, thresholds, and acceptance criteria fixed before evaluation?
Could the result be reproduced independently from retained inputs and versions?
Does the conclusion exceed the scope of the evidence?
Is the same standard applied to favored and disfavored hypotheses?
Could an agent be certifying its own generated work?
